What I want to share

State of AI for development

Because, for real, right now this is how I feel

How last year has felt

Where I’m coming from

  • XP/best-practices approach
  • Ship quality, maintainable software
  • Security practices

How impactful is AI

  • Day to day, small tasks - game-changer
  • Prototypes - revolutionary
  • Autonomous development - flaky claims of success

I’ve been using the agents heavily, to make things easier, but if I give it autonomy, I am compromising on my standards. I have trouble sharing the excitement over openclaw.

And in this context, I’m happily using the tools, but there’s real pressure to use them for more, past my comfort zone, and somehow extract more productivity out of myself. And it’s affecting how positive my attitude is to the whole thing.

Costs of pushing for autonomous development

My experience is that I’m expected to deliver reliable software And if you think about it, claude.ai is more primitive than many MVPs I have worked on. There’s not that much functionality in there.

The choice enterprises need to make

  • Pressure to switch to a new, obscure paradigm
  • Focus on authentic transformations

This leaves a bad taste. And shifts focus in a way that hinders imagination

Weirdly, a lot of the shift for a more positive attitude has come from seeing how product owners go to town with it. I find that very inspiring so I have been thinking a lot about how to reconcile these two perspectives into something actionable.

So I want to claim that instead of pursuing this utopia of infinite features daily, we can focus on very real impactful ways of using it.

Prototyping

  • Without engineering effort
  • Rapid iterations

In the beginning it was a bit intimidating though, because there were all these very nice looking prototypes and we didn’t know where to hide

I have to admit me and my teammates did have a point when we were discussing that, we couldn’t revoke claude access, but maybe ban on gitlab.

But then there was a point when they didn’t have access to some module, but claude coded it from scratch

Prototyping

With AI, we get to do

Deliver a development environment Experiment Play around feel

But the implementation should be thrown away. And that’s not an issue because nobody is attached to it. The agents don’t rant… yet

And building is fine. I know engineers complain about system analysis and security has to be reviewed, but we love doing

Does this mean more features

not necessarily

A lot of the claims about saved development resources and why companies engineers might not feel the pace per se sped up. We look at this and say oh, it would take a lot of time to get the feature right, and we imagine AI coming in and removing these next iterations

But the reality was, a lot of times the company wouldn’t bear the cost of repeated iterations, they would bare the cost of a non ideal feature being deployed, or the feature being scrapped

This is why, if we make all this effort, it’s not always translating to different timelines, but it is translating to better outcomes

Can we extract more value?

Prototypes still take tremendous effort. Can we cascade more of it to rest of the development?

there is one step I haven’t covered before

Prototype =/= Specification

And if you give engineers a prototype, it’s so hard to not look at the code, and copy it, and then the whole mess. But here’s where one of my favorite concepts comes in

What is TDD/ATDD

You first define it in words, then you write the test that checks (the functionality that does not exist), and only then you implement it. it’s not easy but it works beautifully.

go back and redesign

And in engineering context, there’s a lot of different types of tests, but for now we can think of this as automated browser tests.

How can a better flow look like

This is one of the propositions that I have to the whole workflow.

What’s beautiful is that doing tests on prototypes means you do good, implementation agnostic tests. You say “so and so” will happen.

Extended specification

Increase participation in engineering by

  • specification
  • acceptance tests
  • synthetic data

Developers really struggle with this one. This could be a target output for the session, a deliverable for AI. I have had limited attempts for such deliverables in other contexts, and I think the tooling needs to evolve.

What engineering delivers

Accessibility

Not just front-end

Disposable visualizations for back end features can be created with no effort. This is a big shift

Invest in observability and alerting

  • More inclusion, helps undertand the system

  • Assess impact independently
